title: White Oak: Ancient White Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Eastern North America's slow, long-lived oak. Logan, Ohio's is put at roughly six hundred years and still supplies acorns for its own replacements.
intro: White oak is eastern North America's slow, wide-crowned oak, tougher and longer-lived than red oak. The oldest, on the edge of Old Logan Cemetery in Ohio, is put at roughly six hundred years; the town sells saplings raised from its acorns to keep the line going. In Baltimore the Ruxton Liberty Tree was a seedling around 1646 and marked a boundary between two land grants by 1694; the family whose lawn it stands on pays for 5,000 gallons of water a week to keep it alive. At Gettysburg, the Devil's Den witness tree was a sapling when Longstreet's assault opened around it in July 1863. Boston's grows wild on the Arnold Arboretum's Peters Hill, uncatalogued until 2010 and cored in 2018 to roughly two centuries old. Athens, Georgia's is the son of an oak an 1890 newspaper story said legally owned itself.
